answer: The raven graph is rebuilt each epoch, and therefore the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the terrace audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the copper checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 6 times its size, so a group of 29 keys loses far more than 29 single identities would. That is 22 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
